identity.title: Exploring and Mitigating Adversarial Manipulation of Voting-Based Leaderboards

problem.claim: Voting-based LLM leaderboards use human preferences to rank models and are trusted as capability measures.

gap.claim: The paper addresses vulnerability when bot protection and other defenses are not implemented, enabling adversarial leaderboard manipulation.

contributions.claim: A two-step attack identifies the generating model for a reply and then targets voting for or against a selected model.
The authors report that an attacker can alter the leaderboard at roughly the cost of a thousand votes in a simulated, offline Chatbot Arena.
In collaboration with Chatbot Arena developers, the authors identify, propose, and implement defenses intended to increase attack cost.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish their work by demonstrating adversarial manipulation of voting-based benchmarks and implementing mitigations with the Chatbot Arena developers.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report over 95% accuracy for determining which model generated a given reply.
The authors report leaderboard alteration at roughly one thousand votes in a simulated, offline Chatbot Arena.

The authors report that their analysis indicates the mitigations substantially increase attack cost; Cloudflare bot protection, malicious-user detection, and rate limiting predated the collaboration, while reCAPTCHA and login were being integrated.

narrative_sequence.summary: Human voting is increasingly used to evaluate LLM outputs, with Chatbot Arena ranking anonymously paired model responses.
These platforms are described as widely trusted measures of LLM capabilities.
Without adequate defenses, an attacker can identify reply sources with over 95% accuracy and manipulate votes to change rankings at roughly one thousand votes.

The authors collaborated with Chatbot Arena developers to identify, propose, and implement mitigations; Cloudflare bot protection, malicious-user detection, and rate limiting were already present before the collaboration, while reCAPTCHA and login were being integrated.

source_observation.claim: The attack first infers model identity, then uses that information to vote consistently for or against a target.

lessons.interpretation: Separating attribution from manipulation exposes a concrete attack surface in anonymized preference systems.
lessons.application: When analyzing a human-voted benchmark, decompose threats into information leakage and downstream vote manipulation, then test each stage separately.
lessons.exception: This decomposition may be unsuitable when model identity is already public or votes cannot be targeted.

unknowns: The abstract does not report whether the attack works against the live platform or only the simulated offline version.
It does not specify the mitigations' individual effects, attack-cost measurements, or deployment status beyond the stated integrations.
Attacker resources, vote distribution, and statistical significance conditions are unspecified.

editorial_revisions.before: Based on their analysis, implemented and planned defenses substantially increase the cost of attacks.
